reasons: The lake record identifies United States v. Loera, court 10th Cir., decided 2019, with official citation 923 F.3d 907.
The content citation/court/year match the lake identity and citation fields for the reviewed assertion.
residual_risks: The disclosed opinion text caption lists No. 17-2180 while the lake/content docket field lists 17-2087; docket is not part of this assertion.

reasons: The opinion centrally addresses officers encountering evidence outside a warrant's scope while executing a lawful electronic search.

The opinion expressly discusses Horton/plain-view principles and rejects plain view as a justification for the later November 27 search, making the case materially relevant to plain-view limits in digital searches.
residual_risks: The case is also a digital search-scope and inevitable-discovery authority, so its Plain View Doctrine role should not be read as a classic physical plain-view seizure case only.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Label the role as key for digital plain-view/scope limits if the taxonomy allows a narrower home-role note.

defect.problem: The holding assertion overstates the effect of the second pornography warrant. The opinion did not affirm because the agents validly obtained and used that warrant; it held the later searches were unlawful, the second warrant lacked probable cause, good faith did not apply, and suppression was affirmed only on inevitable discovery.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise the holding to keep the need-not-stop rule for Search 1, then state that the November 27 child-pornography-directed search and second warrant failed, but the denial of suppression was affirmed under inevitable discovery.

reasons: The first clause is supported: officers need not stop an electronic search after discovering out-of-scope ongoing-crime evidence if the search remains directed at warrant-specified evidence.

The second-warrant clause is materially misleading because the opinion found the second warrant unsupported by probable cause and affirmed suppression denial on inevitable discovery, not warrant validity.
residual_risks: A narrower proposition limited to the November 20 authorized search would stand.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Split the page holding into separate holdings for Search 1 legality, Search 2/second-warrant invalidity, and inevitable discovery.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, so no treatment merits finding is raised.
The content treatment fields match the lake treatment stub: unverified status, null as-of fields, unverified composite basis, no point overrides, and the same scope note.
residual_risks: No subsequent-treatment verification is disclosed in the lake record.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, so no treatment merits finding is raised.
The authority-weight label is supported by the disclosed identity fields showing a published Tenth Circuit court-of-appeals case.
residual_risks: The label is jurisdictional weight only; it should not imply verified subsequent good-law treatment.
